items.content:
In the lead up to Mother’s Day in the UK, Swiis offices across the country celebrate Every Parent Day, an annual tradition we created to recognise the incredible dedication and hard work of our foster carers who inspire and nurture children and young people every single day.

We launched Every Parent Day to ensure that every person who opens their heart and home feels seen and celebrated. While days like Mother’s Day and Father’s Day celebrate the important role mothers and fathers play within children’s lives, they do not always capture the full, diverse spectrum of foster carers. Every Parent Day is our way of saying that your gender or family structure does not define your impact, your commitment to a child’s life and wellbeing does.

This year’s celebration on the 10th March was a special opportunity for our foster carers to come together with our staff to share a slice of cake, a cup of coffee, and connect with the wider fostering community in their area.

To top off the morning, our foster carers were presented with a gift as a small token of our immense gratitude for the life-changing work they do.

If you have ever thought about fostering, contact our recruitment team, who can answer any questions you have and inform you of the excellent training, support, and financial allowance Swiis offers.

items.title: Sean’s Story as a Young Foster Carer – The Next Generation of Foster Carers
items.snippet: While every foster carer brings different life experiences to the role, the core of fostering remains the same with compassion, commitment, and the willingness to make space in your life for a child who needs it. The post Sean’s Story as a Young Foster Carer – The Next Generation of Foster Carers appeared first on Swiis Foster Care.
items.content:
In 2020, at the age of 32, Sean began a new and meaningful chapter when he and his partner, Chrissy, were approved as foster carers with Swiis. Inspired by seeing the difference a safe and loving home can make for a child in care, they decided to take the step and start the journey themselves.

Starting their journey in their early thirties has allowed them to bring a vibrant energy to a role that has a deeply rewarding outcome. Their story highlights that while every foster carer brings different life experiences to the role, the core of fostering remains the same with compassion, commitment, and the willingness to make space in your life for a child who needs it.

We spoke with Sean about what inspired him and Chrissy to foster, what it has been like caring for children as a younger couple, and the lessons they have learned since beginning their journey with Swiis.

Was there a particular moment, experience, or influence that encouraged you to become a foster carer?

“Our next-door neighbours are foster carers with Swiis, and we spent quite a bit of time with them and the children and young people they cared for, just being out in the garden and spending time together. Chrissy and I both saw the positive impact we were having on the children, even in those small moments out in the neighbour’s garden together, and we thought, we can do this ourselves. We can make a difference.

We have always loved making a difference and seeing people happy, but this felt like a new opportunity to help in a bigger way. It was really rewarding to see our neighbours fostering and to experience that alongside them. It made us think, let’s do this.”

When you decided to go for it, how did your friends and family react to the news?

“They were not surprised at all because we are kind-natured people. They were really supportive, and anyone we asked to be a reference for our application jumped at the chance and was more than happy to help.

Our parents were delighted. They were excited to support us and be part of helping the children and young people we care for, welcoming them into the wider family and making them feel included and happy.”

How long did you think about becoming a foster carer before you took the first step?

“It did not take long at all, about a couple of weeks. After spending time with our next-door neighbours’ foster children, we talked about it for a few weeks and then decided to jump straight in.”

What made Swiis feel like the right agency for you as a younger foster carer? Looking back on your experience so far, what support or training has been the most valuable to you?

“As our next-door neighbour fosters with Swiis, it gave us real insight into the agency. They told us that Swiis is a tier 1 agency, and about the high level of support and care you receive from the staff, which gave us confidence.

That proved to be true. We had Jordon delivering our first few training sessions and he was absolutely brilliant. I felt I could really connect with him. He was honest and genuine, and I thought these are the kind of people I want to work with.

That feeling has carried on with everyone else we have worked with. There are continuous amounts of support and understanding.

Mel, our Supervising Social Worker, is fantastic. She makes you feel like a person and not a number. She has supported us through so much and takes the time to truly understand us and the children and young people we care for. She gives advice and support in whatever way we need.”

Can you share a special memory or moment that made you feel proud of your decision to foster?

“One example happened just last week when we went on our caravan holiday during half term. We had been out all day, and the young girl in our care asked if me and her could go and get an ice cream from the caravan shop when we got back to the caravan site. Which we did, and I bought her an ice cream with flakes on top, and we walked back holding hands.

In that moment, you could see on her face that she was the happiest girl in the world and did not have a care in the world. It was so humbling to know that you have given someone that safe space and that freedom in their mind to just enjoy being a child. That is what it is all about. It is about creating lasting memories that have a real positive impact.

Another example is the boy in our care’s emotional development. We have had him since he was five, and he is now nine. Seeing his emotional intelligence grow and watching him learn to question and understand his feelings at such a young age is incredible.

We have also built a real sense of community with our next-door neighbours. We even went on holiday together last week, and it feels normal and settled for the children. They can pop next door, spend time together, and come back, and it creates a real sense of comfort and belonging.”

Finally, if there is another young person or couple out there who is thinking about fostering but perhaps feels a bit unsure because of their age, what would your advice be?

“If you have a warm heart and good intentions, and you believe you can give a child another chance in life, then just go for it. It is one of the most rewarding things you can do.

It is a privilege to be a parent, and to be able to help children who need that care and support is an even greater privilege.”

For Sean and Chrissy, age is just one part of their story. Whether starting young or later in life, their experience shows that the most important qualities are a warm heart and the desire to have a positive impact on a child or young person’s life. Being part of the children’s development, seeing them laugh, form connections, and create new memories is an experience filled with joy and pride, one that reminds our carers every day how rewarding fostering can be.

If Sean and Chrissy’s journey has inspired you to explore fostering, or if you would like to find out more about becoming a foster carer, contact our recruitment team. They will be happy to guide you through the fostering process, explain the support, training and allowances available, and answer any questions you may have.
